Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Anil Kumar
Hon'ble Rajesh Singh Chauhan,J.
1.
Heard Sri Santosh Kumar Kanaujia, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Ranvijay Singh, learned Additional Government Advocate for the State and Sri Anil Kumar, learned counsel for the complainant.
2. The prosecutrix is present in the Court.

3. As per learned counsel for the applicant, the present applicant (Rehan Ahmad) is languishing in jail since 05.06.2024 in Case Crime No.401 of 2024 under Sections 376, 419, 323, 504, 506, 427 of I.P.C. & Section 3/4 POCSO Act, and Section 3/5(1) of the U.P. entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He has been falsely implicated in this case as he has not committed any offence as alleged in the prosecution story.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the present applicant is an affairs with the prosecutrix and is ready to get married with her.
Since, the applicant and prosecutrix are having different religion, therefore, on account of ill advise the prosecutrix herself lodged an FIR.

Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that an affidavit has been filed on behalf of the prosecutrix wherein this fact has been indicated that she is willing to get married with the applicant and on account of ill advise she lodged the impugned FIR.
5. Attention has been drawn towards Annexure-6 wherein the Investigating Officer has stated that on the basis of educational records the age of the prosecutrix is 17 years 3 months.

6. Further attention has been drawn towards medical examination report of the prosecutrix conducted by the Chief Medical Officer, Lakhimpur Kheri wherein the age of prosecutrix has been determined as 18 to 20 years.

The aforesaid medical examination report is dated 15.06.2024,
therefore, as on today, she has attained the marriageable age even on the basis of educational records.

7. Learned Additional Government Advocate opposed the aforesaid bail application by submitting that at the time of lodging FIR the prosecutrix was minor, therefore, the offence of POCSO was also included in the FIR.

8. Having considered the submissions of learned counsel for the parties and having perused the material available on record; since the prosecutrix is herself present in the Court and has stated that she has no grievance against the present applicant and had lodged the impugned FIR on the basis of ill advise, presently she is ready to get married with the applicant and the applicant is also ready to get married with her, even as per education records the age of the prosecutrix was 17 years 3 months but now she had become major, as per medical examination report conducted by the Chief Medical Officer, Lakhimpur Kheri dated 15.06.2024, the prosecutrix was aged about 18 to 20 years, I find it appropriate that the present applicant may be enlarged on interim bail for a period of four months.
Immediately after releasing on interim bail, the present applicant and the prosecutrix shall apply for their marriage under Special Marriage Act.
Whereafter, the appropriate orders may be passed under the provisions of Special Marriage Act.
If, both the aforesaid parties, got married under Special Marriage Act, they shall registered their marriage before the Marriage Registration Authority.
After getting married with the prosecutrix, the applicant shall look-after her properly, failing which, the interim bail order may be withdrawn on the next date.

9. Accordingly, till the next date of listing, the present applicant (Rehan Ahmad) may be enlarged on interim bail in the aforesaid case crime number, on his furnishing a personal bond of Rs. 50,000/-
with two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-

2 (i).

That the applicant shall make himself available for interrogation by the police officer as and when required;
(ii). that the applicant shall not, directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade from disclosing such facts to the court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence;

(iii). that the applicant shall not leave India without prior permission of the court;
(iv). that the applicant shall not pressurize/ intimidate the prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with evidence during trial (v).
that the applicant shall appear before the trial court on each date fixed unless personal presence is exempted (vi).

that in case of breach of any of the above conditions the court below shall have the liberty to cancel the bail;
(vii). that in default of any of the conditions mentioned above, the learned counsel for the State shall be at liberty to file appropriate application for cancellation of interim bail granted to the applicant.
10. List this case on 2nd December, 2025.

On that date, the applicant and prosecutrix shall appear in person alongwith relevant documents showing that they have got married or those records showing that they have taken proper legal steps to get married.
11. This interim bail order may be extended on the next date or may be made absolute considering the conduct of the present applicant.

(Rajesh Singh Chauhan,J.)
